'''Stanisław Zaremba''' (3 October 1863 – 23 November 1942) was a Polish [[mathematician]] and engineer.<ref name="Ku180">{{harv|Kuratowski|1980|p=180}}.</ref> His research in [[partial differential equation]]s, [[applied mathematics]] and [[classical analysis]], particularly on [[harmonic functions]], gained him a wide recognition. He was one of the mathematicians who contributed to the success of the [[Polish School of Mathematics]] through his teaching and organizational skills as well as through his research. Apart from his research works, Zaremba wrote many university textbooks and [[monograph]]s.

He was a professor of the [[Jagiellonian University]] (since 1900), member of [[Academy of Learning]] (since 1903), co-founder and president of the [[Polish Mathematical Society]] (1919), and the first editor of the ''[[Annales de la Société Polonaise de Mathématique]]''.

He should not be confused with his son [[Stanisław Krystyn Zaremba (mathematician)|Stanisław Krystyn Zaremba]], also a mathematician.

==Life and career==

Zaremba was born on 3 October 1863 in [[Romanivka, Bereznehuvate settlement hromada, Bashtanka Raion, Mykolaiv Oblast|Romanówka]], then part of [[Austria-Hungary]] (present-day [[Ukraine]]), to Hipolit, an engineer,<ref name="Ku180"/> and Aleksandra ({{nee|Kurzańska}}).<ref name="Domoradzki">{{cite web|url=https://pau.krakow.pl/PKHN-PAU/pkhn-pau-XI-2012-5.pdf |language=pl |title=Stanisław Zaremba (1863-1942). Fragmenty biografii w 120-lecie doktoratu |trans-title=Stanisław Zaremba (1863-1942): Excerpts from Biography on the 120 Anniversry of Doctorate |work=Polish Academy of Learning |author=Stanisław Domoradzki |page=82 |access-date=15 July 2026}}</ref> He was educated at a [[grammar school]] in [[Saint Petersburg]] and studied at the Institute of Technology of the same city obtaining his diploma in engineering in 1886.<ref name="Ku180" /> 

The same year he left Saint Petersburg and went to [[Paris]] to study mathematics. He received his doctoral degree from the [[University of Paris|Sorbonne]] in 1889<ref name="Ku180" /> based on his dissertation ''Sur un probleme concernant l'etat calorifique d'un corps solide homogene indefini'' written under the supervision of [[Gaston Darboux]] and [[Émile Picard]].<ref name="MathGen">{{cite web|url=https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=12546 |title=Stanislaw Zaremba |work=Mathematics Genealogy Project |access-date=14 August 2026}}</ref> 

During his stay in [[France]], Zaremba established close scientific contacts with [[Paul Painlevé]] and [[Édouard Goursat]]. Another French mathematician, [[Jacques Hadamard]], observed that Zaremba's work enabled overcoming difficulties that mathematicians had been struggling with for years. The generalizations introduced by Zaremba reshaped the foundations of [[potential theory]] and other areas of [[mathematical physics]], becoming the starting point for intensive work by a new generation of mathematicians on [[hyperbolic equation]]s, the [[Dirichlet problem]], and [[harmonic function]]s.<ref name="Wójcik"></ref> 

He left France in 1900 and joined the faculty at the [[Jagiellonian University]] in [[Kraków]] taking over the chair of mathematics. His years in France enabled him to establish a strong bridge between Polish mathematicians and those in France. In 1905, Zaremba was awarded the title of full professor by the Jagiellonian University.<ref name="Koroński">{{cite web|url=https://repozytorium.biblos.pk.edu.pl/redo/resources/29782/file/suwFiles/KoronskiJ_StanislawZaremba.pdf |title=Stanisław Zaremba (1863‒1942) and His Results In the Field of Differential Equations |work=Technical Transactions |date=2015 |author=Jan Koroński |access-date=14 August 2026}}</ref> 

In 1919, he was one of the founding members of the Kraków Mathematical Society, transformed the following year into the [[Polish Mathematical Society]].<ref name="MacTut">{{cite web|url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Zaremba/ |title=Stanisław Zaremba |work=MacTutor History of Mathemitics Archive |author=J.J. O'Connor, E.F. Robertson |access-date=14 August 2026}}</ref> According to [[Władysław Ślebodziński]], Zaremba played a vital role in shaping the Golden Age of mathematics in Poland during the [[Interwar period]].<ref name="MacTut"></ref> He is also regarded as a leading representative of the [[Kraków School of Mathematics]].<ref name="PolRad"></ref>

His notable students included [[Stanisław Gołąb]], [[Wacław Sierpiński]], [[Włodzimierz Stożek]], and [[Witold Wilkosz]].<ref name="MathGen"></ref> Zaremba served as Vice-President of the [[International Mathematical Union]], and was a member of the [[Polish Academy of Learning]] (1903)<ref name="Wójcik"></ref> as well as a corresponding member of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] (1925).<ref name="Domoradzki"></ref>

He died on 23 November 1942 in [[Kraków]], during the [[History of Poland (1939–1945)|German occupation of Poland]].

==Work==
Zaremba's research was primarily centered on [[partial differential equation]]s and [[potential theory]]. In addition, he made substantial contributions to [[mathematical physics]] and [[crystallography]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Zaremba/ |title=Stanisław Zaremba |work=mathshistory-st-andrews |access-date=1 July 2026}}</ref>

Zaremba, together with [[David Hilbert]], introduced around 1900 the [[direct method in the calculus of variations]], a general technique for proving the existence of minimizers of a given [[functional (mathematics)|functional]] drawing on methods of [[functional analysis]] and [[topology]].<ref>{{cite book | last = Dacorogna | first = Bernard | title = Direct Methods in the Calculus of Variations | publisher = Springer-Verlag | year = 1989 | isbn = 0-387-50491-5 | pages = 1–43}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |title=Calculus of Variations |author=I. M. Gelfand |author2=S. V. Fomin |year=1991 |publisher=Dover Publications |isbn=978-0-486-41448-5}}</ref>

Another notable result by Zaremba, introduced in 1907, is the [[reproducing kernel Hilbert space]],  which pertains to [[boundary value problem]]s for [[Harmonic function|harmonic]] and [[Biharmonic equation|biharmonic functions]].<ref>Zaremba, S. L’équation biharmonique et une classe remarquable de fonctions fondamentales harmoniques. Krakauer Anzeiger, 147-196 (1907)</ref><ref name="Koroński"></ref>

In 1910, Zaremba solved the first boundary value problem involving a [[mixed boundary condition]] for the [[Laplace's equation]].<ref>{{cite journal | last = Zaremba | first = S. | year = 1910 | title = Sur un problème mixte relatif à l'équation de Laplace | journal = Bulletin international de l'Académie des Sciences de Cracovie. Classe des Sciences Mathématiques et Naturelles, Série A: Sciences mathématiques | language = French | page = 313 | jfm = 41.0854.12}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ucm.es/garf/file/clnv14?ver |title=THE ZAREMBA PROBLEM IN TWO-DIMENSIONAL LIPSCHITZ GRAPH DOMAINS |author=Maria Jusus Carro, Teresa Lugue, Virginia Naibo |work=Universidad Complutense de Madrid |access-date=14 August 2026}}</ref>

===Research activity===
{{blockquote
|text= Zaremba's magnificent discoveries found a broad response and deep appreciation in the world. Stanisław Zaremba is the pride of Polish science. At the same time, by his pioneering activity in such an important field as mathematical analysis, he became one of the creators of modern Polish mathematics.
|sign= [[Kazimierz Kuratowski]]
|source= {{harv|Kuratowski|1980|p=183}}.
}}

==Recognition==
In 1908, Zaremba became the first Polish mathematician to have the privilege of giving an invited talk at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Rome]].<ref name="PolRad">{{cite web |url=https://polskieradio24.pl/artykul/2624248,stanislaw-zaremba-matematyk-ktory-zadziwil-europe |language=pl |title=Stanisław Zaremba. Matematyk, który zadziwił Europę |trans-title=Stanisław Zaremba: The Mathematician Who Amazed Europe |work=polskieradio24 |author=Danuta Ciesielska, Krzysztof Ciesielski |access-date=2 July 2026 |date=23 November 2025}}</ref> He is among the most frequently invited mathematicians to this conference, having received this honour five times.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?page=180 |title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers |work=mathunion.org |access-date=2 July 2026}}</ref>

In 1925, he was awarded the Commander's Cross of the [[Order of Polonia Restituta]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dziennikustaw.gov.pl/M1925262108201.pdf |language=pl |title=Monitor Polski |work=dziennikustaw.gov.pl |access-date=1 July 2026}}</ref> Three years later, he was decorated with the French [[Legion of Honour]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=Domoradzki |first=Stanisław |date=2012 |title=Stanisław Zaremba (1863–1942). Fragmenty biografii w 120-lecie doktoratu |url= |trans-title=Stanisław Zaremba (1863–1942). Excerpts From Biography on the 120th Anniversary of Doctorate. |journal=Prace Komisji Historii Nauki PAU |language=pl |location=Kraków |volume=11 |publisher=Polska Akademia Umiejętności |access-date= |page=79-102}}</ref> In 1936, he received the [[Cross of Merit (Poland)|Gold Cross of Merit]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://isap.sejm.gov.pl/isap.nsf/DocDetails.xsp?id=WMP19362630464 |language=pl |title=M.P. 1936 nr 263 poz. 464 |work=isap.sejm.gov.pl |access-date=1 July 2026}}</ref> Zaremba also received honorary doctorates from [[Aix-Marseille University|University of Aix-Marseille]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://jbc.bj.uj.edu.pl/dlibra/publication/edition/94645 |language=pl |title=Prof. Zaremba doktorem h.c. Uniwersytetu w Marsylii |work=jbc.bj.uj.edu.pl |access-date=1 July 2026}}</ref> [[Jagiellonian University]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uj.edu.pl/uniwersytet-z-collegium-medicum/nagrody-i-wyroznienia/dhc |language=pl |title=Doktorzy honoris causa |work=uj.edu.pl |access-date=1 July 2026}}</ref> and the [[Adam Mickiewicz University]] in Poznań.

In 1982, the [[Polish Post]] issued a 5-[[zloty]] commemorative stamp featuring Zaremba as part of the "Polish Mathematicians" series.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://katalogznaczkow.net/matematycy-polscy-2688/ |language=pl |title=Matematycy polscy – 2688 |trans-title=Polish Mathematicians - 2688 |work=katalogzanczkow.net |access-date=1 July 2026}}</ref>
